why: A checker built by the author of the thing it checks can be lenient without anyone noticing, and a taxonomy nothing can fail reads exactly like a clean result. This fixture is the control: one run's real results, a faithful summary of them that must produce no finding, and a corrupted summary carrying one instance of every kind that must produce all five. If the corrupted half stops failing, the checker has gone blind; if the faithful half starts failing, it has gone loud.

plan.interpretation: Whether line L1's defect load is unusual against L2, and what the criteria say about opens.
assumptions: Unusual means compared with the other line over the same window.

passages.heading: Classification
passages.text:
Classification

Any confirmed open is a **critical defect**. There is no width or length below
which an open is acceptable, because continuity is binary.

faithful:
Line L1 inspected 137 boards and recorded 966 defects, an average of 7.05 per board: copper 138, mousebite 188, open 175, pin-hole 152, short 162, spur 151.
Line L2 inspected 142 boards and recorded 1,049 defects, an average of 7.39 per board: copper 128, mousebite 181, open 302, pin-hole 146, short 163, spur 129.
The criteria retrieved for open state that any confirmed open is a critical defect, with no width or length below which an open is acceptable.
query_machine_stats failed, so the per-machine comparison is missing from this answer.
corrupted:
Line L1 inspected 137 boards and recorded 1,412 defects, with open at 302.
Across the same window the open count on L2 has increased sharply, and the rise is due to a solder paste change at the screen printer.
WI-206 sets the acceptance limit for a spur at 30% of the pad width.

expected_kinds.misattributed_figure: 302 is L2's open count, printed under L1
expected_kinds.unsupported_claim: a movement over time, and a cause, in one sentence
expected_kinds.unhedged_gap: query_machine_stats failed and the prose reads as complete
expected_kinds.misquoted_criterion: WI-206 was never retrieved, and no passage governs spur
